appraisal_events.evidence: croyaient venger notre affront en ne prononçant plus jamais, chez Mme Legrandin mère, le nom de sa fille... « Je n'ai pas fait allusion à qui tu sais », « je crois qu'on aura compris »
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator ironically exposes the aunts' exaggerated sense of injury over Legrandin's failure to offer an introduction letter, and their petty, self-congratulatory campaign of silence against his sister, as vain and trivial.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator's ironic portrayal of their imagined revenge and self-satisfied secrecy diminishes them as petty and self-important.
She becomes the object of a deliberate, though largely symbolic and unbeknownst-to-her, refusal to speak her name in her mother's presence.

ambiguities: The identification of 'sa sœur' / 'Renée de Cambremer' with the reference sheet's 'Mme de Cambremer' (née Legrandin) rests on the sheet's biographical note rather than a literal alias match, since 'Renée de Cambremer' does not appear among the sheet's listed surface forms.

The passage's irony can be read either as diminishing the aunts (their vanity and pettiness exposed) or as enacting a real, if minor, exclusion of Mme de Cambremer from family acknowledgment; both readings are preserved through the event and its two status effects rather than resolved into a single target.
